definition: A device that provides additional USB connection points or helps extend a USB connection beyond a standard cable length.
A particle of light whose quantum properties, including polarisation, can be used in quantum key distribution.
The restriction of a photon's light vibrations to particular directions, used to represent and measure quantum information.
A quantum key distribution method that uses randomly chosen polarisation bases and later compares basis choices.
A television accessory containing an embedded computer system that manages receiving, recording and playing television content.
A light-sensitive semiconductor component that converts incoming light into an electrical signal.
An input device that measures a solid object from multiple spatial directions to build a digital three-dimensional model.
A projector that uses liquid-crystal display technology to form an image and project it onto a larger surface.
Data representing a physical quantity that changes continuously rather than taking only discrete values.
Data represented by discrete values, typically binary digits, so a computer can process it.
A sensor that transmits and detects an infrared beam and reacts when an object interrupts the beam.
A sensor that detects infrared heat radiation emitted by nearby objects without needing to transmit a beam.
A separately developed section of source code that can be combined with other modules to make a complete program.
A computer or service that hosts website files and supplies requested web pages to browsers over a network.
A programmable processing component that interprets sensor readings and determines control signals for output devices or actuators.
An index or address identifying the current top item of a stack; it changes when items are pushed or popped.
An index or address identifying the base of a stack, remaining fixed during the stack operations illustrated in the book.
An index or address identifying the next queue item to be removed by a dequeue operation.
An index or address identifying the rear of a queue, updated as new items are enqueued.
